raw_evidence.quote: Use the !include directive to include file in your diagram. Using URL, you can also include file from Internet/Intranet. ... Imagine you have the very same class that appears in many diagrams. Instead of duplicating the description of this class, you can define a file that contains the description. ... By default, a file can only be included once. You can use !include_many instead of !include if you want to include some file several times. Note that there is also a !include_once directive that raises an error if a file is included several times.

How could I paint relations containing 'composed keys', a relation between multiple columns in both classes? Foo2::(column2,column3,column4) --> Foo1::(column2,column3,column4). I only know how to paint relations between individual class members, for example Foo2::column1 --> Foo1::column1

named_subset_views_over_one_model.rationale: PlantUML does have a genuine named-subset-of-source-text mechanism: authors wrap named blocks in !startsub NAME / !endsub inside one source file, and a separate diagram file pulls in only the named block(s) via !includesub. This is real, documented grammar, not user convention. However, it is a TEXT-inclusion mechanism operating on line ranges tagged by the author, not a model-aware VIEW mechanism: it has no concept of 'entity', 'relationship', or 'this entity's neighbours' the way Structurizr's views do. To produce a readable subset diagram of, say, 6 of 25 entities and only the relationships among them, the author must manually decide which lines belong to which named sub-block and manually keep the tags in sync as the model evolves — there is no query like 'give me EntityX and everything within 1 hop.' The materially different, and more commonly used, alternative documented on the same page is !include of a shared file containing entity definitions, then writing several independent top-level @startuml/@enduml diagrams that each include a different combination of shared files — i.e., several separate diagram files sharing common entity text, not named views computed over one single source model. Both routes exist and are recorded distinctly; neither is a semantic view mechanism, so this is classified as expressible-only-via-workaround rather than expressible.

contrary_evidence_search.result: Found: a real but text-level (not model-level) named-subset mechanism (!includesub), and a separate, materially different multi-file composition mechanism (!include of shared entity definitions across independent diagram files). NOT found: any PlantUML feature described as a 'view', 'viewpoint', or model-aware filtered projection in the terminology Structurizr uses. NOT found: any built-in composite-key, multi-column UNIQUE, or cross-cutting-convention construct anywhere searched (consistent with, and reusing the same negative finding as, source-plantuml-ie-notation.json). This record's overall unresolved gap: whether the parser rejects a relationship referencing an undeclared entity (vs. silently auto-creating an empty box for it) was not confirmed against a primary source within this session — flagged identically in source-plantuml-ie-validation-exit.json as the single most important open question for the semantic-validation research question, since it bears directly on whether PlantUML could ever be extended into a genuine schema-consistency gate.
